title: Guard Clause and Early Exit
definition: A guard clause handles an invalid, exceptional, or boundary condition near the start of a flow and exits that flow before the main path continues.
purpose: Reduce unnecessary nesting and keep the normal path visually and conceptually direct.
history: Guard clauses are a long-standing structured refactoring technique for replacing nested conditionals.
mental_model: A security checkpoint rejects disallowed cases at the entrance so the inside procedure can focus on admitted cases.
analogy: An entrance check; it fails when early exits scatter cleanup responsibilities or hide required side effects.
common_mistakes: Using a guard without naming the rejected case
industry_notes: Guard clauses improve clarity when they expose boundary cases; they can harm clarity when exit points are unstructured or lifecycle obligations are hidden.
ai_notes: Require before-and-after path tables and tests for AI-proposed guard-clause refactors.
interview_notes: Ask when early return clarifies a function and when it creates risk.
exercise_candidates: Prove equivalence with a decision table
